title: Two external measures

blocks.heading: Two external measures
blocks.text: Balance of trade is export value minus import value for goods over a period; balance of payments records wider economic transactions between residents and non-residents. State explicitly if a supplied trade measure includes services. An investment inflow is not itself a goods export and cannot automatically be counted as an improved goods trade balance.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Balance of trade
blocks.text: Balance of trade is the value of goods exported minus goods imported over a stated period. Exports above imports give a surplus; below give a deficit. Use comparable currency, period and scope rather than combining counts and values.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Balance of payments
blocks.text: Balance of payments is a record of economic transactions between a country’s residents and non-residents over a stated period. It includes more than goods trade, such as services, income, transfers and financial flows. Detailed sub-account accounting is outside this lesson.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Use the evidence
blocks.text: A fictional country records annual goods exports of N$75 million and goods imports of N$68 million. Exports minus imports gives a goods trade surplus of N$7 million. This balance excludes services and financial transactions, so it is not a complete measure of external payments or development. A separate investment inflow must not be added as if it were a goods export.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
